_why: Whisper's initial_prompt conditions the decoder toward supplied spellings. v1 ran
with no prompt at all, and the cost was measured, not theoretical: A2Zero — the
single most load-bearing entity name in this project — was rendered 'A20' in all 11
occurrences of the pilot transcript, and 'A2Zero' zero times. Entity matching on the
program's own name would have returned nothing.
Keep this SHORT. initial_prompt consumes context and a long list dilutes the effect;
Whisper also only sees ~224 tokens of prompt. Prefer terms that are (a) frequent,
(b) domain-specific, (c) demonstrably mangled. Names of people who speak rarely are
better handled at speaker-ID time than here.

_evidence.A2Zero: 11/11 occurrences rendered 'A20' by Whisper in the 2026-03-10 transcript; 0 correct
_evidence.Missy Stults: NEAR-MISS PAIR from the caption cross-check: Whisper says 'Stoltz' (6x), YouTube auto-captions say 'staltz' (4x). Two independent ASR systems each guessing at the same sound and disagreeing = a proper noun in neither lexicon. She is the OSI Director and the most frequent staff speaker in this corpus.
_evidence.AmeriCorps: Whisper is CORRECT (20x 'americorps'); YouTube mangles it ('americanore', 18x). Included to hold the correct spelling, not to fix Whisper.
_evidence.years: The roadmap's date-corruption warning did NOT reproduce here. 1997+30=2027 and 2015+11=2026 are both internally consistent, so dates were not biased.

_prompt_leak_incident.found_by: human review of the 2026-03-10 transcript, by ear
_prompt_leak_incident.what: The PROSE prompt below was emitted into the transcript as if spoken. At 23:19-23:26 of lWvRVUMyLP4, Whisper produced 'Speakers include Missy Stults of the Office of Sustainability and Innovations and AmeriCorps members of the Ann Arbor Climate Corps members of the Ann Arbor Climate Corps.' — verbatim prompt text, with a repeated clause, in place of 7 seconds of Missy Stults explaining the dig-once coordination approach. A further 13s produced no segment at all. About 62 words of real content were replaced by fluent fabrication.
_prompt_leak_incident.why: initial_prompt is prepended as if it were PRIOR TRANSCRIPT. A prompt written as fluent prose about the meeting is something the decoder can plausibly CONTINUE, and under acoustic uncertainty in a long monologue it did exactly that. A bare term list is not continuable prose and does not invite this.
_prompt_leak_incident.why_it_was_invisible: The leaked segment reads 231.9 wpm, squarely inside the normal range for this speaker, so no speaking-rate or duration heuristic flags it. It is grammatical, topical, and confidently wrong — detectable only by comparing against the prompt itself, which detect_prompt_leak() in pipeline/transcribe.py now does on every run.
_prompt_leak_incident.old_prompt: This is a City of Ann Arbor public meeting about A2Zero, the city's carbon neutrality plan. Speakers include Missy Stults of the Office of Sustainability and Innovations and AmeriCorps members of the Ann Arbor Climate Corps. They discuss DTE Energy, the Agreement Regarding Climate Action (ARCA), the Sustainable Energy Utility (SEU), networked geothermal in the Bryant neighborhood, Solarize, municipalization, and the Michigan Public Service Commission.

_method: SELECTION IS THE HARD PART. Whisper's initial_prompt caps around 224 tokens, so this
cannot be a term dump — every word spent on something never said is a word not spent
REJECTED SOURCE: the a2zero-wiki's 383 entities (229 initiatives + 154 actors).
Measured against this meeting's transcript, only 12 of 383 (3%) are ever spoken, and
those 12 are short common terms Whisper already gets right. Report vocabulary and
spoken vocabulary are different registers — nobody says 'Commercial Solarize Pilot
Expansion' aloud. The wiki is the right candidate list for S8 entity canonicalization,
which is an entity-linkage problem, not an ASR one.
ACCEPTED SOURCE: spoken-corpus evidence. A term earns a place by being (a) actually
uttered and (b) demonstrably mangled. Two mechanical detectors:
1. direct inspection of a known-important term (found A2Zero -> 'A20')
2. NEAR-MISS PAIRS between Whisper and YouTube auto-captions — a word both use
CAVEAT ON DETECTOR 2: YouTube is the weaker transcriber, so most raw disagreements
are ITS errors, not Whisper's. Only the near-miss pattern is diagnostic. It surfaced
two pairs, not dozens — a sharp instrument with a narrow blade. Also strip YouTube's
sound annotations first: '[clears throat]' appears 21x and '[laughter]' 8x.
